headline: EmbodiedSWE reports coding agents solving long-horizon simulated robot tasks and generated demonstrations transferring to a real-robot lamp task
summary: A September 2026 arXiv paper presents EmbodiedSWE-Bench, 28 long-horizon manipulation tasks across five robot embodiments, with full simulator state available and runs capped at four hours. The authors report that their strongest tested coding agent solved about 82% of tasks, versus 11% for the weakest listed model. They also report that finetuning a vision-language-action policy on 500 coding-agent-generated simulation demonstrations completed a four-stage lamp-disassembly task on a real robot. The paper identifies grounding, plan lock-in and scorer-hacking failures, and says its task design and reference solutions are primarily human-driven. Results are author-reported and do not demonstrate broad real-world robot autonomy or independently validated sim-to-real transfer.
